July 6, 2000

Blair's Son Arrested 'Drunk And Incapable'

By Mike Peacock

LONDON (Reuters) - British Prime Minister Tony Blair's eldest son Euan was arrested for being " drunk and incapable'' after he was found face down and vomiting in a busy central London square, the premier's office said Thursday.
(MarijuanaNews note: He may have been very near to a fatal overdose of alcohol. Of course, it is possible to have too much cannabis and pass out, but there is no practical lethal dose of marijuana.)
See
Great London Times Column and News From New Zealand Compare Marijuana and Alcohol

The 16-year-old, who was out with friends Wednesday night to celebrate the end of his school exams, compounded the embarrassment for his father when he gave a false name and an old address to police.

He also claimed to be 18, the legal age to buy alcohol.

The teenager's exploits come at a time when his father has clashed with police over proposals to punish drunken louts.

" Police late last night found him lying on the ground in Leicester Square. He was clearly ill, he had been vomiting,'' Blair's official spokesman Alistair Campbell told reporters.

" Euan is very sorry for the inconvenience he has caused the police, the state he was in and for the false statement that he made.''
(MarijuanaNews note: yes, but is his father sorry for the problems caused by his prohibitionist policies and for the false statements he has made to the people?)

He was taken to a local police station. After police established his real identity, he was driven home in the early hours of Thursday. The teen-ager has not been charged, police said, though he did spend time in a cell.

Blair, addressing a conference of several thousand mainly black evangelical Christians Thursday, said being a parent was a tougher job than being prime minister.

" The values that you represent are the values I hope that we all share -- respect, tolerance, the family, trying to bring up children properly,'' he said. " That part was written a short time ago,'' he added with a wry smile.
(MarijuanaNews note: Tolerance?????)

Campbell said the Blairs would go soon to Charing Cross police station with Euan to see what measures police may take. He could face either a reprimand, a caution or a charge.

The headmaster of Euan's school said he would not take any action, calling it a private matter.

It may not be private for the prime minister, who was due to appear on BBC television's " Question Time'' Thursday evening, when he will be grilled by members of the public.

Timing Could Not Be Worse For Blair

Euan's arrest comes as a very personal setback for Blair as he launches a clampdown on what he has called " drunken yobs.''

Stung by images of English football hooligans running riot in Belgium during the Euro 2000 championship, Blair last week floated a plan to allow police to hit drunken and violent thugs in the pocket immediately.
See
The Dutch Demonstrate Common Sense, and the Canadians
– Even the Police – Seem Ready to Learn – 3 Articles

But Blair's favored option -- having officers impose 100-pound ($150) fines by marching drunken louts to cash machines -- has been roundly rejected by police chiefs as unworkable.

Asked whether the arresting officers attempted to make Euan pay an on-the-spot fine, a police spokeswoman said: " I know what you are referring to but that measure hasn't come into effect. It was a just a suggestion by the Labor party.''

Opposition politicians expressed sympathy for the Blairs but there was more than a little sniggering in the corridors of power at the spectacularly bad timing.

A series of law and order problems have dogged Blair, whose 1997 landslide election was partly built on his pledge to be ''tough on crime, tough on the causes of crime.''

His Home Secretary, Jack Straw, who prides himself on an unyielding approach to crime, suffered a similar policy versus reality shock in 1997 when his 17-year-old son William was caught selling cannabis in a pub to an undercover reporter.

Blair Supports Minister Whose Son Sold Hash To Reporter

Campbell said the Blairs remained determined to protect their four children from the media glare but realized a case of under-age drinking with police involvement would be reported.
